title: Would You Take a $10K Raise If It Meant 60 Hours a Week?
script: Everyone says yes to the $10K raise. Nobody does the math. $10,000 extra per year sounds great. But spread across 500 extra work hours — that's roughly $20 per hour extra. If your current hourly rate is already $50 an hour, you're taking a pay cut. And research shows that beyond 50 hours a week, your productivity doesn't just slow down — it collapses. Three questions to ask before you say yes: What is my actual hourly rate after this? What is this costing my health and relationships? And can I negotiate the terms instead of just accepting the trade? More money isn't always more value.
